name: Orange County 2024–25 district comparison
model_scope: Orange County independent 2024–25 grade-school district models: exact operational CCD LEA 1201440 / native FL-48 attachments, complete reported pure lower offerings including grade 3–8, and explicit-zero native enrolled grades 9–12. Exact attached charters, alternatives and special-education profiles are retained; native missing outcomes determine eligibility. Separate same-year native Florida School Grades Math, ELA and Combined point-only OLS models. High and mixed offerings are excluded.
map_source: School coordinates and district boundaries are unavailable in the audited Orange sources.

income_definition.label: Individual reported FRPL/direct-certification eligibility
income_definition.definition: Florida 2024–25 Final Survey 3 (February) raw individual Lunch Status counts: D/F free eligibility + 3/E reduced eligibility + C/R CEP direct certification, divided by same-survey enrolled students (PK–12). Never uses the USDA 1.6-adjusted federal funding numerator or published school-grade economic percentage. CEP N means not individually identified eligible and is excluded from the numerator. Provision 2 code 4 reports all enrolled students, so schools with nonzero or masked code 4 have unavailable income. At CEP schools this proxy counts direct certification/household extension rather than a complete income survey of all families; undercount and reporting coverage are unknown. No other-year backfill.

cohorts.assessment: Florida School Grades FAST + FAA + Math EOC · grade schools
cohorts.grades: Grade schools: FAST3–8, FAA, Math EOC and source-attributed students
cohorts.standard: 2024–25 native School Grades English Language Arts Achievement and Mathematics Achievement components: Level 3 or above / valid assessed students under Florida full-year-enrollment and home-zoned attribution rules, including eligible FAA Performance Task but excluding FAA Datafolio. ELA FAST PM3 grades 3–10 and Math FAST PM3 grades 3–8 plus B.E.S.T./Access Algebra 1/Geometry EOCs; this cohort enrolls no grades 9–12 in the same-year Survey 2 registry. ELL included after two US-school years; medical/extraordinary exemptions excluded. Components require at least 10 eligible students. Native whole-percent rates only; score denominators absent, so all model sampling intervals unavailable. Collocated combined results and provider-specific virtual rates are excluded from individual-school matches.

policy.roster: Exact operational 2024–25 CCD LEA 1201440 / FL-48 attachments only; retain the full 282-record directory, 275 operational identities and 268 native profiles. Pure offered inventory 209 includes 207 tested configurations; 208 profiles match native sources.
policy.populations: Require complete reported pure PK–8 offerings, at least one offered grade 3–8, and explicit zero native Survey 2 enrollment in every grade 9–12. 206 matched profiles are offered-applicable; two matched PK-only profiles are nonapplicable. The unmatched 48-1961 offers 6–8 and remains a missing native profile, never a primary-only or inferred zero-income profile.
policy.native_eligibility: Independent subject eligibility uses same-year raw individual lunch income and native Florida achievement exclusions; 200 eligible schools per subject. Preserve all exclusions and native-usable mixed 48-0283 outside the pure cohort.
policy.source_exclusions: Retain seven missing-Fall schools, two primary profiles, collocated 48-0042/0065 shared 17 Math/20 ELA evidence and five other missing pure campus outcomes. The original 61-row CCD membership proof is discovery evidence only, never a fit or native eligibility filter.
policy.zero_income: Eligible charter 48-0056 and 48-0061 retain verified zero recorded individual lunch eligibility and positive February enrollment. Zero recorded eligibility is not evidence that no low-income families attend. Never trim these members by income or influence.
policy.school_types: Retain exact attached-LEA charter, alternative and special-education flags. Native exclusions leave 182 noncharter and 18 charter Regular schools eligible; no fit-driven exclusions.
policy.models: Separate 2024–25 native Florida full-year/home-zoned School Grades Math, ELA and Combined ES district OLS; never reuse statewide residuals.
policy.studentization: Externally studentized residuals use deleted-school residual scale with N−3 degrees of freedom.
policy.intervals: Point estimates only: native valid-score denominators are absent. Counts, sampling variances and all interval endpoints remain null, modelwide. An internal zero variance vector is a computational sentinel, never an uncertainty estimate.
policy.combined: Equally weighted mean of eligible Math and ELA proficiency; not percent proficient in both. No counts or sampling variance are inferred.
policy.release: Numerically verified audit only; source and modeling approval remain false pending independent review and separate canonical/browser integration.

# of CEP Direct Certification with USDA Multiplier
- This value is the total from the school-level report where the CEP Direct Certification USDA multiplier was applied. This count represents the sum of the numbers in the Column “# of CEP Direct Certification with USDA Multiplier” found on the Lunch Status School-Level report.
- When all students in a school are reported under Direct Certification (Codes C & R), the USDA multiplier of 1.6 is applied to the total number of Direct Certification students (C & R).
- If the calculated number exceeds the total school enrollment (membership), it is capped at the membership value.
- Important note: If the school also reports students under the free/reduced-price lunch categories or Provision 2 category, and Direct Certification students are included, the multiplier will not be applied to those students.

# of Free or Reduced-Price Lunch with USDA Multiplier if Applicable (Numerator)
- This number reflects the total count of students reported with specific lunch status codes (D, F, 3, E, 4, R, or C). If the USDA multiplier is applicable to the school, this count will include the Direct Certification students multiplied by 1.6. This count represents the sum of the numbers in the Column “# of Free or Reduced-Price Lunch with USDA Multiplier if Applicable (numerator)” found on the Lunch Status School-Level report.
- If the USDA multiplier is not applied to a school, this number will simply reflect the raw count of students reported under the lunch status codes (without the multiplier).
- If the USDA multiplier is applied, it reflects the adjusted count, which includes the Direct Certification students and their 1.6 multiplier.

Two PK-only profiles are nonapplicable; six applicable profiles have unavailable outcomes, including one excluded collocated campus aggregate. All 200 eligible schools are regular: 182 noncharter and 18 charter. Verified zero recorded individual eligibility at Lake Eola and Hope Charter remains 0%. methodology.summary: Orange County independent district grade-school models with same-year individual lunch eligibility.
details: Orange County independent 2024–25 grade-school district models: exact operational CCD LEA 1201440 / native FL-48 attachments, complete reported pure lower offerings including grade 3–8, and explicit-zero native enrolled grades 9–12. Exact attached charters, alternatives and special-education profiles are retained; native missing outcomes determine eligibility. Separate same-year native Florida School Grades Math, ELA and Combined point-only OLS models. High and mixed offerings are excluded.

Every subject uses an independent district OLS fit and externally studentized residuals. Filters do not refit it, and statewide Florida residuals are never reused. Associations do not establish causal school effectiveness or overall quality.

The discovery screen has 206 potential grade schools, matching the 206 native source-applicable profiles; independently verified source income/outcomes support 200 model members. Planning never selects model members. Full pure offered inventory 209 includes 207 tested configurations, while matched source scope 208 includes 206 applicable profiles. The original 61-row CCD membership proof retains all seven missing-Fall and both primary-only schools; reported-zero CCD membership never creates native income or outcomes.

All 208 matched pure lower profiles stay in the directory, including two PK-only nonapplicable schools and six applicable schools with unavailable achievement. Unmatched 48-1961 offers 6–8 and remains in source coverage without an invented Fall profile. High/mixed offerings, all seven unmatched operational records and the complete nonoperational roster remain retained. Native-usable mixed 48-0283 is excluded by offered scope, not performance.

The offered-grade population requires complete reported PK–8-only flags, at least one offered grade 3–8, and explicit-zero Survey 2 enrollment in all grades 9–12. Protected positive counts never mean zero. All 206 matched applicable profiles have positive or protected tested-grade enrollment; raw offered/enrolled differences remain auditable.

Collocated campus rows 48-0042 and 48-0065 share group 480042480065 and published 17 Math/20 ELA. Those aggregate rates cannot be assigned to each campus individual income. The pure campus 48-0065 remains excluded with the raw evidence preserved.

Eligible charter 48-0056 (Lake Eola) and 48-0061 (Hope) have explicit zero recorded individual lunch eligibility and positive February enrollment; their income remains 0%. Zero recorded eligibility does not establish that no low-income families attend. No school is trimmed by income, influence or anticipated fit.

2024–25 native School Grades English Language Arts Achievement and Mathematics Achievement components: Level 3 or above / valid assessed students under Florida full-year-enrollment and home-zoned attribution rules, including eligible FAA Performance Task but excluding FAA Datafolio. ELA FAST PM3 grades 3–10 and Math FAST PM3 grades 3–8 plus B.E.S.T./Access Algebra 1/Geometry EOCs; this cohort enrolls no grades 9–12 in the same-year Survey 2 registry. ELL included after two US-school years; medical/extraordinary exemptions excluded. Components require at least 10 eligible students. Native whole-percent rates only; score denominators absent, so all model sampling intervals unavailable. Collocated combined results and provider-specific virtual rates are excluded from individual-school matches.

Florida 2024–25 Final Survey 3 (February) raw individual Lunch Status counts: D/F free eligibility + 3/E reduced eligibility + C/R CEP direct certification, divided by same-survey enrolled students (PK–12). Never uses the USDA 1.6-adjusted federal funding numerator or published school-grade economic percentage. CEP N means not individually identified eligible and is excluded from the numerator. Provision 2 code 4 reports all enrolled students, so schools with nonzero or masked code 4 have unavailable income. At CEP schools this proxy counts direct certification/household extension rather than a complete income survey of all families; undercount and reporting coverage are unknown. No other-year backfill.

The outcome, Fall grade registry and February income describe different prescribed populations. Whole-percent achievement rounding and incomplete CEP income eligibility remain limitations. Published economic percentages, enrollment, percent tested, letter grades and the ten-student publication floor never supply valid-score denominators.

Combined is the equally weighted mean of eligible Math and ELA proficiency, not proficiency in both. Counts and sampling variances are unavailable and no interval endpoints are published for any member of any district model. External studentization uses each deleted-school residual scale; it provides no enrollment adjustment or shrinkage.

Independent full fits and every leave-one-out fit were verified. Maximum leverage is 0.031433; deleting one member changes a fitted line by at most 1.048 proficiency points across observed income. Lake Eola has the maximum ELA/Combined Cook distance and stays included with income 0%. Conventional influence flags are descriptive, never reasons to discard schools or assign quality labels.

This is a single-year grade-school comparison. No audited admissions classifications, coordinates or boundaries are supplied. State assessment standards and economic eligibility do not create an interchangeable national scale.
